intro: This course raised awareness of anxiety, its common forms, and how to support people with warmth while signposting them towards professional help.
points: This is awareness only — you recognise, support and signpost, but you never diagnose or treat, and anxiety is treatable with the right help.
Escalate urgently — any mention of self-harm or feeling unable to cope must be raised straight away.
Remember a panic attack is frightening but not dangerous, and the feelings will pass — stay calm, reassure, and encourage slow breathing.
Never tell an anxious person to simply "stop worrying" — acknowledge how real the feeling is and listen without judgement.
Encourage a conversation with the GP as the usual first step, since people can often self-refer to NHS talking therapies too.
Record changes in mood, sleep or behaviour factually, and look after your own wellbeing so you can keep caring well for others.
